item.title: Tata Sons board members to visit Air India HQ, review performance on Nov 19
item.description: Tata Sons board members, including Chairman N Chandrasekaran and Noel Tata, will be visiting Air India headquarters in Gurugram on Thursday, according to sources. Air India is co-owned by Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines, which holds a 25.1 per cent stake. The sources said the members will be reviewing the performance of the loss-making Air India. The airline's MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam will be making a presentation to the members, they added. Besides, operational integration of Air India and Air India Express is likely to be discussed, the sources said. Tata Sons Chairman Chandrasekaran, board member Noel Tata and others will be visiting the Air India headquarters on Thursday, they added. It could not be immediately ascertained whether all the Tata Sons board members will be visiting the airline's headquarters. item.title: Tata Steel plans project to produce hydrogen using steel plant off-gases
item.description: Tata Steel, in partnership with Houston-based Utility Global, will undertake a project to produce hydrogen using steel plant off-gases at its Kalinganagar facility in Odisha, marking the first such initiative in the country, the company said on Wednesday. The two companies will undertake joint Front-End Engineering and Design (FEED) studies to support a Final Investment Decision (FID) by Tata Steel's board on the proposed project, it added. The proposed facility, based on Utility Global's H2Gen technology, will have a planned capacity of 10 tonnes per day (TPD) and use off-gases generated during the steelmaking process to produce high-purity hydrogen. "For any technology to make a meaningful contribution to steel decarbonisation, it needs to work at the scale and complexity of an operating steel plant. Technologies like H2Gen give us the opportunity to pursue emissions reduction while leveraging the existing infrastructure. Our collaboration with Utility Global marks another pivotal

item.title: SpiceJet board approves ₹5,500 crore fund raising proposal for revival
item.description: Struggling SpiceJet's board on Wednesday approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to shore up its financial position. The airline has been facing multiple headwinds, including financial and operational woes. At its meeting on Wednesday, the airline's board was apprised of investment discussions with potential new investors. The board has cleared the proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to strengthen the airline's financial position, rebuild capacity and drive its revival, according to a statement. Further, the board has directed the management to work towards closing it expeditiously. "The proposed fundraise may be undertaken through a combination of equity and other permitted instruments and will be subject to the requisite approvals," the statement said. Besides, the board has approved increasing the company's authorised share capital from Rs 2,000 crore to Rs 7,500 crore, subject to the necessary shareholder and regulatory approvals.
